name: Personal Public Service Number (PPS No)
note: Ireland's sheet (its government's own sheet on the OECD's automatic-exchange portal ('Information on Tax Identification Numbers'; the OECD's index page sits behind a bot check and wasn't opened, the sheet itself came straight back)), read 2026-10-30: the Personal Public Service Number is issued by the Department of Social Protection and used by the Revenue Commissioners to identify taxpayers; it is issued automatically on birth registration for children born in Ireland, and anyone else applies at a Department office; never changed. The sheet's format is seven digits and one or two letters; the pattern draws the one-letter form (the two-letter form is not modelled). Read as given at birth, to residents. No check rule, fee or time is stated.

sources.title: OECD AEOI portal, Ireland: Information on Tax Identification Numbers (the jurisdiction's own sheet)
sources.said: The number used to identify taxpayers is the Personal Public Service Number (PPS No). This number is issued by the Department of Social Protection ... PPS-numbers are issued automatically on birth registration for children born in the country. Anyone else must make application at an office of the Department of Social Protection. ... 7 digits + either 1 or 2 letters.
